earlier_scan.source_named: Only descriptive source, Z'graggen 1969 PhD (ANU, read in full text), explicitly omits stress: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' No other source exists.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. x+335 pp. hdl:1885/130077
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Same survey-wide sentence, p. 13 (PDF p. 22): stress marking omitted because 'the stress patterning has not been well established yet'. Wadaginam 35/Wd treated as in the 1971 book; nothing language-specific on stress.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: OLAC listing for wdg (language-archives.org/language/wdg; archived copy (Internet Archive, 28 Dec 2025)) -- to confirm whether SIL-PNG holds any unpublished Wadaginam item (survey wordlist, alphabet-design worksheet, organised phonology data)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only unchecked catalogue; if an SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet or survey report exists for Wadaginam it would be the first source to state stress. Nothing of the kind surfaced in Glottolog, TNG, NGW or web searches.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World: 'Tomui River' and 'Wadaginam' pages (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch), last modified 2024
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; historical segmental phonology only (e.g. *s varies [t ts s] in Wadaginam). Its Sources section confirms Wadaginam data come only from Z'graggen 1971: 72 and 1980: 1-80. The Wadaginam page itself is an empty stub.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2015. A reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: phonology, lexicon, and morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. (and the revised book: Daniels 2020, Grammatical Reconstruction: The Sogeram Languages of New Guinea, De Gruyter Mouton, p. with the same passage)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentioned only as a source of comparative pronoun/lexical forms taken from Z'graggen 1980; no phonology or prosody of Wadaginam.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don R. 2010. A preliminary phonological history of the Sogeram languages of Papua New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 49(1): 163-193. University of Hawai'i Press. DOI 10.1353/ol.0.0068.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: nothing; passing mention only (listed p.164 as external to Sogeram with obligatory noun number suffix and *k lenition per Z'graggen 1980d, Pawley 1998a, Barrett 2005; one form ni- 'eat' cited p.190 from Z'graggen 1980d:72). The paper's only stress statement (p.168 'Stress is almost always word-final in the daughter languages') is scoped to the eight Sogeram languages, all already read.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Southern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-33. Canberra: ANU. xvi+97+10 pp. (Wadaginam = G7)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Intro sec. 9 (p. ix): transcription 'rendered semi-phonemic'; secs 10, 13, 14 mention Wadaginam only for noun number suffixes, verbal object prefixes and y->g in 1pl/du pronouns. The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur; G7 forms carry vowel length but no stress marks (visual check pp. 4, 8).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; sec. 2.8.2.2.2.4.4 (pp. 584-585) is classificatory (family-level isolate across the Goam River, socially tied to Tangu). No occurrence of 'stress' in the chapter.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: Australian National University. vi+154 pp., map. hdl:1885/146484
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: no phonology content: checklist of languages with codes, classification, villages and census figures, and an index of language names; the strings stress/accent/tone/tonal/phonolog do not occur.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C19 (Wadaginam = language 35 'Wd'; sec. 2.22.32 p. 59; Josephstaal Stock typology sec. 2.22.36 pp. 60-61; transcription note sec. 1.3.3 p. 6)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey-wide only (p. 6): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Wadaginam section (p. 59) and Josephstaal typological features (pp. 60-61: stops, prenasalisation, nasals, fricatives, /r/ vs no /l/, vowels incl. high central, number marking, possessive classes, affix order) say nothing about stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1970. Languages of the Western Madang District. In S. A. Wurm and D. C. Laycock (eds), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, pp. 1271-1292 (+ maps). Pacific Linguistics C-13. Canberra: Australian National University. hdl:1885/253814
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Only prosodic content: 'None of the languages appears to be tonal' (Adelbert Range Phylum, which includes Wadaginam). Segmental typology (velar nasal, high central vowel, velar fricative), possessive-class and verb-affix-order features; no stress/accent statement, no transcriptions of Wadaginam words beyond the charts.
